description:
Honeysuckle (Lonicera spp.) is a common garden vine or shrub. Some parts, especially the berries, can be mildly toxic to cats if eaten.

The plant may contain saponins and, in some species, compounds that can release small amounts of cyanide-like chemicals. Cats usually do not eat large amounts, but berries can be easier to swallow than leaves or stems.

A cat that eats honeysuckle berries or leaves may vomit, have diarrhea, drool, or seem uncomfortable. Keep fallen berries cleaned up and do not let cats chew the plant. Contact a veterinarian if your cat eats a large amount, symptoms repeat, or your cat seems weak.
